steps.text: Wind Chimes, Wind Chimes!
Phew, managed to catch you before you left town.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Ah Yun? What's wrong? Did I leave something at the post office?

steps.name: Ah Yun
steps.text: It's not that. The mandarins want a letter sent to Shiqiao Village.

steps.name: Ah Yun
steps.text: But none of the Messengers at the post office had ever heard of a place by that name, so they spent a while asking around.

steps.name: Ah Yun
steps.text: Not sure how this came up, but eventually someone said 'if Wind Chimes doesn't know, then I reckon nobody knows.'

steps.name: Ah Yun
steps.text: And that was just as you'd left.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Got it. I'll take care of it.
Wind Chimes threw open her rucksack, revealing the various letters stuffed to the brim within.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Just throw the letter in there. I've heard of Shiqiao and roughly know which direction it's in, but I might have to ask for specifics along the way.

steps.name: Ah Yun
steps.text: Where are you going after you finish your deliveries? Yumen or Lungmen?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Lungmen. Lungmen's had a longer backlog of letters to be delivered to the mountain countryside than Yumen.

steps.name: Ah Yun
steps.text: Then, I'll treat you to that new Mrs. Pepper ice cream that's been all over the ads when you get back. Apparently, they're going the spicy-and-savory route this time, and it's not sweet at all!

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: But, isn't ice cream supposed to be sweet?

steps.name: Ah Yun
steps.text: Pssh. When you get tired of eating sweets, you obviously go with something spicy. That's what's trendy these days.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Leaving the on another delivery run?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Mmhmm.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Go right on ahead then, no search needed. When I saw you taking every single letter out and neatly packing them back in, I felt a bit bad for inconveniencing you.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Appreciate it.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Oh, also, Old Cheung asked me to thank you for him.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Cheung?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: That bearded guy whose letters kept bouncing because his hometown was relocated.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: You delivered several dozen of his letters all at once, and when he got some replies back, he was so happy he started crying.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Oh, I remember now... It's not like I did anything special. Just part of my job.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Then, thank you for doing your job. You take care of yourself now!
After staying in a nomadic city for a while, people tend to forget that there is an 'outside'.
But, the 'outside' is actually pretty close. Close enough that if you walk a few li out towards the edge of the tracks, you'll come face-to-face with the wind and sand.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Thanks for your hard work on fixing up the Chidao!

steps.name: Humble Worker
steps.text: Oh, if it isn't the Messenger with the broken horn! What's up? Did we get mail? Is it for me, or some young lad or lass on our construction site?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I do have mail, but it's just a stipend from Lungmen.

steps.name: Humble Worker
steps.text: A stipend, huh...?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: You don't seem too thrilled about it.

steps.name: Humble Worker
steps.text: No, of course I am! The whole point of comin' out here to work is to make life a little better! I'm just, a bit worried. It's been two months since we've gotten any letters from our village.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I passed by the village just last month. Everyone was very nice.

steps.name: Humble Worker
steps.text: That's good to hear.

steps.name: Humble Worker
steps.text: Say, don't be in such a rush to leave. Stay here for dinner, and leave some time tomorrow.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I have a lot of mail to deliver this time, so I think I should––

steps.name: Humble Worker
steps.text: Don't be shy, we're practically family here! Everyone's always looking forward to you coming around. It's mighty interesting hearing you talk about the cities.

steps.name: Humble Worker
steps.text: Since we got paid our stipends today, I'll have 'em get the food ready for you earlier, and find some youngsters for you to chat with!

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Next.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Leaving for work?

steps.name: Well-Traveled Man
steps.text: Yes, work.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Please open your bag for security inspection.

steps.name: Well-Traveled Man
steps.text: Oh, right, there's something I wanted to ask.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Well-Traveled Man
steps.text: Did a Forte Messenger with a broken horn leave the city at about noon today? Would you mind telling me which way she went?

steps.name: Impatient Villager
steps.text: 'Jianzi... rumian... I'm in Lungmen...'

steps.name: Impatient Villager
steps.text: Ah Fang, you know how to read, don't you? C'mere and help me figure out what this says.

steps.name: Exhausted Villager
steps.text: What is this thing anyway, a flashlight? I already have one at home. Why would they need to send one out from Lungmen?

steps.name: Young Villager
steps.text: Auntie, that's not a flashlight, it's a telescope!

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: What's this?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: It's a camera. I use it to document everyone's lives.

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: You mean, the stuff they use to make TV shows?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Uhh... close enough?

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: Then, I'd better clean myself up and make a good impression...
Other people always say you become numb after working for too long. They say this is true for everything else as well, that everything becomes normal once you've been through it enough.
But when I go back and forth between the mountains and the cities, what I deliver most is letters back home.
There's hardly any difference between this month's letters and last month's. Just a few extra days of rain, a few extra bushels of wheat harvested.
But as long as their home remains, people will continue to write letter after letter.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Oh right, would you happen to know how to get to Shiqiao Village?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I only know that it's somewhere to the north, but don't know the exact location...

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: Shiqiao? Can't say I've ever heard of it. Want me to try asking around?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I'd appreciate it.

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: Sorry, but we don't know either.

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: But, apparently there's a lad in Bianti who came from Shiqiao, seeking shelter with his relatives. He might know the way.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Bianti Village? Sounds good. I happen to have mail to deliver there as well.

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: You're not going to stay awhile?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Not this time. See you around!

steps.name: Suspicious Man
steps.text: Hey you, old timer!

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: Hmm? What's wrong?

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: Wait, who are you? I haven't seen you around here before.

steps.name: Suspicious Man
steps.text: The Messenger that was here just now, did she say she was going to Shiqiao?

steps.name: Curious Villager
steps.text: Yes, but... Hey, are you just gonna leave without saying anything?

steps.name: Suspicious Man
steps.text: My home is close to Shiqiao. I'll lead her there!

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: A boy from Shiqiao...? Wait, do you mean Ah Liang?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: Get over here, Ah Liang! Someone here needs directions!

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Head north, then about ten li after reaching Beifen, there's a big tree several arms' length 'round. Enter the mountains from there.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: After turning around, there'll be a two-way trail. Follow it all the way to the right for about a day...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Alright, got it.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: You can memorize something that complicated?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Actually... Following the trail to the left leads you to my hometown.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: I'll just say this, you look just like one of us country folks, like you're right outta the mountains.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: By the way, how's your hometown doing? Has everything been alright?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: It's deserted. Everyone's already moved into the city for work.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: *sigh*... The last few years have been tough, and our village has been through similar, but at least we've managed to survive. Be careful out there.

steps.name: Crafty Man
steps.text: Excuse me, that Messenger just now–

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: Did you have some business with her?

steps.name: Crafty Man
steps.text: I'm also trying to get to Shiqiao Village. I heard you folks talking about it from the distance, but I didn't catch everything...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: There's Beifen.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Two letters to be delivered here in Beifen, then one last letter... to Shiqiao.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Why are there so many people gathering here?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: They're all here to... read the announcement?

steps.name: Rushed Villager
steps.text: Yeah, our village's finally gettin' relocated. There's a new nomadic plate that's lookin' for workers, and they say anyone who helps build it can help keep it runnin' after the plate's been completed.

steps.name: Rushed Villager
steps.text: If the notice has been posted, doesn't that mean the convoy's probably ready to pick us up in a few days?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: What about your mail...?

steps.name: Rushed Villager
steps.text: Just hand it over to me. I'll make sure to pass it out when everyone gets back. Really appreciate you bringing us our letters all these years.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: ...You're welcome.

steps.name: Rushed Villager
steps.text: Huh? What are you still headin' north for?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I have one last letter addressed to Shiqiao.

steps.name: Rushed Villager
steps.text: Shiqiao Village?

steps.name: Rushed Villager
steps.text: They were supposed to get relocated last month. Dunno if anyone's there anymore.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Are you... absolutely certain about that?

steps.name: Rushed Villager
steps.text: Certain I saw the news. It was nailed up on the announcement board. The convoy also went into the mountains a few days ago, but we haven't seen any cars leavin'...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I might still be able to make it then.

steps.name: Rushed Villager
steps.text: I wouldn't, if I were you. It's a long ways out, you don't even know if there'll be anyone there, and you might even get robbed–

steps.name: Rushed Villager
steps.text: Huh? Where'd she go?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I appreciate the tip, but I need to get going. There should still be enough time!
As the sun sets, the mountains stretch out along both sides of the narrow road.
Just past ten li north, I saw the dead tree. I followed a few bends and went into the mountains, climbing over peaks and ridges until I reached a fork in the road.
This is the way I went out, back in the day, but this time...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Excuse me, you're in the way.

steps.name: Suspicious Man
steps.text: Sorry, but we're here for the letter.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I don't have anything addressed to you in this bag.

steps.name: Suspicious Man
steps.text: Is that so? Well, I heard you had something for Shiqiao. The village is just ahead, so hand it over and I'll deliver it for you.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I'm good.

steps.name: Suspicious Man
steps.text: Hmph, so you wanna play hardball, huh?

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Hand the letter over. It's just one piece of paper. Stop wasting time and bring it here!

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Make me.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Oh, you have the guts to challenge us? Think you're hot shit, huh?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Have we met before?

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Cut the crap! The boss ain't around this time, so don't expect us to show any mercy!

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Your stance looks pretty good by-the-books, but let's see if your blade has ever tasted blood...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Gah!

steps.name: Crafty Robber
steps.text: You're pretty quick on your feet––

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Hyah!

steps.name: Crafty Robber
steps.text: Shit, this wench means business!

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: What are you afraid of? She can't take all of us at once!

steps.name: Crafty Robber
steps.text: Why's a little errand runner putting her life on the line? You sure as hell don't know what's good for you.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: (Pants) ...I have nothing to say to you.

steps.name: Crafty Robber
steps.text: (Whispers) Laoge, she's not backing down. Maybe we ought to...

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: (Whispers) Hmph, that's our only option now.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Why don't we all take a step back? I'll tell you exactly why we can't let you through, and then you decide whether or not it's worth fighting us.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Do you know whose letter you're delivering? Our boss sent it after he got arrested.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Shiqiao is the boss's hometown, and that place has been deserted for a long while now. If not for the fact that you were going around where it was, we wouldn't have had eyes on you.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: As if I'd believe you.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Sure, so we fight you to the death over a piece of paper from who-knows-where. Does that even make any sense?

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Lemme give it to you straight: before he got caught, the boss hid some treasure. If he went through all the trouble to send that from Lungmen, there's gotta be something big inside.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: So hand over the letter, and when we find the treasure, we'll split it with you.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: In your dreams.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Alright, then. Let me just tell you one more thing. We were the ones who saved your life. Your horn wasn't broken back then, and you weren't carrying that blade on your back.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: You what–?!

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Does that jog your memory?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: You're... those first group of robbers that I met? The ones who blindfolded me and burned my letters?

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Who else?

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: If not for the fact that the boss didn't wanna cause extra trouble and felt sorry for the pitiful little girl who lost her family, you think taking the head of a mandarin is some big deal?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Pitiful? What about that is pitiful?

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Heh, do you actually think we had any pity for you?

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Any thieves worth their salt are already striking it rich in some nomadic city. If we had somewhere to go, you think we'd be camping out in these barren mountains to rob people?

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: You might even call this destiny, that you're here again delivering the boss' letter. Now that we're meeting again after so many years, let's not make this an ugly occasion.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: (Shakes head) If you really think this is destiny, you'd best get out of my way.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: What, don't you speak Yanese?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I bought this blade after you robbed me. Don't make me use it on you.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: You heard her, boys. Since you've got a death wish, don't blame us for what happens next.

steps.name: Crafty Robber
steps.text: You'd dare?!

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: ––Hyaaah!

steps.name: Crafty Robber
steps.text: She's protecting that bag! Stab her in the back!

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Her reactions are pretty quick...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: You'd best... leave while you can. Those two back there aren't fatally injured. You could save them.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: We've already given you the bottom line. If you're not gonna cooperate, we can't let you leave here alive.

steps.name: Crafty Robber
steps.text: Your legs have gone weak, girl. Behave yourself and hand over that letter. Come with us, and you might even make yourself a fortune.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Don't... even think about it...

steps.name: Crafty Robber
steps.text: Look at you. You can't even finish a sentence––

steps.name: Crafty Robber
steps.text: Urkh...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I was aiming... for your arm. Don't expect... the same courtesy next time.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Not bad. A single Messenger managed to take down three of us. But, that's the best you can do. Put your blade down.

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: I said, put your blade down!

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: What the hell? You brought backup?!

steps.name: Arrogant Robber
steps.text: Run, run!

steps.name: Well-Traveled Man
steps.text: Are you alright?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I... I'll manage. Who are you?

steps.name: Well-Traveled Man
steps.text: That letter...
Wind Chimes takes a step back.

steps.name: Well-Traveled Man
steps.text: Sorry, I got ahead of myself. Here's my ID.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: The L.G.D.?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Long story short, I have some work to take care of, and I'd like your cooperation. Come back with me to Lungmen, and wait for us to finish inspecting this letter before you send it out.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: What's the deal... with this letter?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: This letter was sent by a bandit leader we had in custody. He said it was a letter home to his mother in Shiqiao Village.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: We looked into his claim and found that he indeed was from Shiqiao. By the way, the first crime he confessed to was robbing you.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: The guy's never been back home since he left, and it's been over a decade. Given that he doesn't have much time left, we didn't really try to stop him.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: He hasn't been back home in a decade?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: He claimed it was to avoid getting his family involved, but as for the actual reason... Who knows?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Unfortunately, at around the same time you left town, we discovered that he had been involved in a rash of related cases.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: And so we had to consider the possibility that what he sent wasn't a letter to home, but rather a message.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: But... I'm almost there. What are the odds that this whole thing is a misunderstanding and it really is just an ordinary letter to home?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: I followed you all the way here just to confirm that.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Sir, if you follow this fork to the right, it'll take you to Shiqiao. If you follow it to the left, it'll take you to my hometown... But, you won't find anything there anymore.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Shiqiao will be relocated soon. I still know where to address my letters home, but this man...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Do we have to go back to Lungmen?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: *sigh*... If you're dead set on not going back, then I suppose I can inspect the letter right here.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: But, if there really is some funny business going on with this letter, or if something happens to me, you'll be held liable.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: That's fine.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Even though that guy robbed you?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: This has nothing to do with that case, but...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Someone who's been away from home that long, and won't ever be able to go back... I want to believe that his last letter was just an ordinary letter home.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Alright then.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Does that camera of yours work? If so, I'd like you to take pictures of the entire inspection process.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: ...And, done.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: So... What's the story...?
The man folds the letter neatly, stuffs it back inside the envelope, and then hands the envelope back to me with a pat on the shoulder.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Go ahead and send it where it belongs.
I know that on the other side of this mountain lies more mountains, and that when the convoy from Shiqiao sets out, they'll at best meet me head-on. But, I can't slow down.
It feels as if I'm rushing to meet the last of my neighbors who still haven't moved.
If I arrive earlier, we'll be able to sit down together for a chat over a cup of tea. Any later, and I'll only be able to catch the sight of their backs.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: *pant*, *pant*... Finally made it...

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: Who might you be, girl? Are you here to see off your relatives?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: No, I'm... a Messenger. I have a letter to Shiqiao from Lungmen...

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: Lungmen? It mustn't have been easy coming all the way out here. Let me see that letter, and I'll ask the people who've already boarded.

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: Well, that's unfortunate. This letter seems to be addressed to Aunt Zhao.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Unfortunate?!

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: Don't panic. It's not what you think. Aunt Zhao is fine. She's old and a bit addled, but otherwise fine.

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: The villagers made an agreement that everyone would leave together once the convoy arrived, but now she's refusing to leave, throwing a childish fit and saying we lied to her.

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: I'm not sure if she'll be able to read your letter.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Regardless, let's get it delivered to her first.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: ...Auntie?

steps.name: Addled Elder
steps.text: Who's there? Who is it this time? I said, I'm not leaving! I don't care about nomadic cities or telephones or intercity nets– it's all a scam!

steps.name: Addled Elder
steps.text: You're all trying to trick me into leaving, just like you tricked Erya! I'm not going anywhere!

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I'm not here to ask you to leave. I simply came to deliver a letter–

steps.name: Addled Elder
steps.text: I'm not leaving! I'd rather die than leave! I'm just going to wait right here... I don't like sweets!

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Addled Elder
steps.text: Who are you? How'd you get into my house?

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I'm a Messenger, Auntie. I've come to deliver a message from your son–

steps.name: Addled Elder
steps.text: I don't know how to read, and I've been lied to and cheated my whole life... But, what's the use? Erya knew how to read and write, but he was cheated all the same...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: I believe Erya wrote this letter for you.

steps.name: Addled Elder
steps.text: Letter...? What letter? He's never written home before...

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: How about this: I'll read his letter for you, okay?

steps.name: Addled Elder
steps.text: Read the letter... for me?

steps.name: Addled Elder
steps.text: Yes, please.

steps.name: Wind Chimes
steps.text: 'I'm sorry, Ma. I haven't been back home in more than ten years. I haven't even sent a single letter...'

a.text: I'm sorry, Ma. I haven't been back home for more than ten years. I haven't even sent a single letter.
I don't want to be a burden on you, and I also don't know what I should even write.
I went down the wrong path and hurt a lot of people. I've been living in a stupor the last few years, as if I've gotten terribly sick.
People say that you have to choose your own path, and can only rely on yourself. But, I'd rather rely on the hawkers who'd come to the village. You could always trust them to bring ice cream.
It was so sweet, Ma. Even after all these years, I still remember that taste. Whatever that stuff was labeled 'ice cream' on the outside, how could anything be so sweet and so delicious?
I used to love jujubes. But after that, I wouldn't even touch the biggest, reddest jujubes. I just wanted to eat ice cream.
You scolded me back then. Said I was acting like I was possessed. Maybe I really was possessed, and ended up ran away from home over some ice cream.

When I first made some cash of my own, I immediately went and bought a whole box of ice cream with all sorts of different flavors. But, I ate until my stomach was upset, but still couldn't taste that same maddening sweetness.
Now that everything's said and done, I don't think I'll ever be able to go home again. But, don't worry about me. I'll be fine.

If you really miss me, just go plant a jujube tree behind the house and pretend that it's me. In the spring, when the tree sprouts new leaves, that means I've woken up. In the autumn, when the jujubes fall to the ground, it's me who ate them.
If the thorns on the jujube tree prick you, it means I'm throwing a fit. You can hit me or scold me, but my roots will always be there. I won't go anywhere. I'll always be with you.
I guess that's it. Think of that as me coming back home.

steps.text: When I get to the end of the letter, I have to grit my teeth to keep myself from crying. But, the old woman simply turns around, slowly making her way to the backyard.
There is already a carefully tended tree in the center of the courtyard, covered with jujubes both green and red.
The old woman slaps her palm down between the branches and leaves of the jujube tree, and the sharp thorns dig into her hand. Tears crawl down her wrinkled face.
After a moment of silence, she turns around and heads in the direction of the convoy.
